title: Rabbi Zakkai of Kabul
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:5: “Rabbi Chinena bar Andrai in the name of Rabbi Zakkai of Kabul: If he erred between one word and another, they make him go back.” Hyman cites Tanchuma, Shemini 3, for an incident involving one of the leading men of Kabul (Hyman proposes this reading, as in Vayikra Rabbah 20:3) who was marrying off his son. The son went up to the upper room, where a snake bit him… Rabbi Zakkai of Kabul came in and delivered a eulogy for him. Hyman thinks it very likely that the account near the beginning of Semachot, chapter 8, in which Yehudah and Hillel, the sons of Rabban Gamliel, went to Ben Zakkai in Babylonia, should perhaps read “to Rabbi Zakkai in Kabul.” This requires investigation.

notes.text: Saved Vilna digital Semachot 8 has the sons of ר״ג, and saved Machon Mamre Tosefta Moed Katan 2 fully writes Rabban Gamliel. The supplied ר״נ and parenthesis רב רבי remain disclosed rather than fabricated as “our Rabbi.” Hyman’s Kabul-for-Babylonia conjecture explicitly requires investigation, and that genuine source question keeps the notice held.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. I, p. 401) gives ר״ג (בר רבי). The supplied digital text has ר״נ (רב רבי), as recorded in the earlier note. Vayikra Rabbah 20:3 reads Kabul and ends with Rabbi Zakkai’s quotation of Ecclesiastes. In the Torat Emet Tanchuma, the story appears in Shemini 2, with Babylonia and a plural closing attribution. Yitzchok Lowy’s digital Tanchuma gives Kabul and has Rabbi Zakkai enter and open with the verse. The Vilna Semachot at 8:4 gives Ben Zakkai in Babylonia, while the Soncino English gives Ben Zakkai at Kabul. In Tosefta Shabbat 8:8 (Machon Mamre), the sons of Rabban Gamliel go to Kabul and the townspeople honor them with wine and oil flowing through pipes. That parallel supplies the town and the custom. Hyman’s proposal about the host remains conjectural.
